title: Reinforcement learning to improve large language model-based automated code compliance systems
abstract: arXiv:2606.22402v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based approaches for automated code compliance (ACC) of building regulations are prone to generating incorrect and hallucinated computer-processable rules. This paper introduces P4IR, a two-stage framework that uses supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to instill domain knowledge in an LLM, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to improve the accuracy of the generated intermediate representations in the form of high-level code skeletons. The framework achieved final reductions of up to 21.3% and 41.0% in tree edit distance and token-level Levenshtein distance respectively, relative to the SFT baselines. Comparative analysis demonstrates that this approach in a zero-shot setting outperforms leading LLMs in both code structure and semantics, evaluated via few-shot prompting. Additionally, the GRPO stage produced a statistically significant reduction in false positives. By combining SFT with GRPO

translated_title: 基于强化学习改进大语言模型的自动规范合规系统
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的建筑法规自动合规检查（ACC）方法容易生成错误和幻觉的可计算机处理规则。本文提出了P4IR，一个两阶段框架：首先使用监督微调（SFT）向大语言模型注入领域知识，随后通过组相对策略优化（GRPO）来提高以高级代码骨架形式呈现的中间表示的生成准确性。相对于SFT基线，该框架在树编辑距离和词元级Levenshtein距离上分别实现了高达21.3%和41.0%的降低。对比分析表明，该方法在零样本设置下，在代码结构和语义两方面均优于通过少样本提示评估的领先大语言模型。此外，GRPO阶段在统计上显著降低了误报率。通过将SFT与GRPO相结合
tldr: 本文提出P4IR两阶段框架，通过监督微调（SFT）注入领域知识并结合组相对策略优化（GRPO）强化学习，显著提升了大语言模型生成建筑法规合规规则的准确性，将树编辑距离和词元级Levenshtein距离分别降低达21.3%和41.0%，并统计显著地减少了误报。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes P4IR, a two-stage framework combining supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) reinforcement learning, which significantly improves the accuracy of LLM-generated computer-processable rules for automated building code compliance, reducing tree edit distance by up to 21.3% and token-level Levenshtein distance by 41.0% while statistically significantly decreasing false positives.
